newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan halts Taiwan pork imports, eyes other sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan halts Taiwan pork imports, eyes other sources.

text.p: Japan on Friday said it will stop pork imports from Taiwan indefinitely due to an outbreak of the foot and mouth disease among the hog population there, but stressed that no immediate impact is likely on domestic supplies.
Local meat traders, however, said they have boosted their pork buying from alternative sources, particularly the United States, as domestic prices have already started to rise.

On Thursday, Taiwan banned all pork exports following an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease in its hog population, spelling huge losses for one of the island's top export industries.

Japan's import ban will be in place for at least six months, and will apply to all pork slaughtered after February 21. Japan is the largest export market for Taiwanese pork, which is mainly used for making sausage.
"We don't expect any immediate impact on domestic supplies because of larger-than-usual stocks here," said Akinori Aonuma, director of the Agriculture Ministry's Animal Health Division.

At the end of January, Japan had 172,000 tonnes of pork in storage, including both locally produced and imported meat, ministry data showed. Stock levels of between 80,000 and 90,000 tonnes are regarded as sufficient.
Japan's pork demand in the fiscal 1995/96 year ended March was 1.461 million tonnes, and of that, Taiwanese origin accounted for 249,000 tonnes or 17 percent, the farm ministry said.
Between April 1996 and January 1997, Japan imported about 620,000 tonnes of pork, and Taiwanese meat accounted for 244,000 tonnes of that, it said.
Despite the government's optimistic view, local traders said they are on the alert as domestic pork prices have already crept up on Friday, affecting their talks with U.S. sellers.
"It is a seller's market now. The U.S. exporters are waiting for prices to rise further before concluding deals," a pork trader at a major trade house said.
Traders said they were also eyeing pork from Canada and the European Union.

Another farm ministry official said that Japan had no plan to alter its current "emergency" import tariff on pork, which was put in place to protect local breeders and was recently extended until June.
"We're going to keep the special pork tariff until this June as announced earlier. This has nothing to do with the import ban on Taiwanese pork," the official said.
